title: MS Dhoni Invests in Rooftop Solar Startup SolarSquare, Named Brand Ambassador
excerpt: The former India cricket captain invested through his family office Midas Deals as part of SolarSquare's $53 million Series C round, which valued the Mumbai-based company at up to $500 million.
body:
• MS Dhoni has invested in SolarSquare through his family office Midas Deals, joining the company's $53 million Series C funding round.
  • Dhoni has been named SolarSquare's brand ambassador, marking another clean energy bet from the former India captain's growing startup portfolio.
  • The Series C, led by B Capital with participation from Lightspeed and others, takes SolarSquare's total funding past $100 million at a valuation of up to $500 million.
  • SolarSquare plans to expand into 30 to 40 new cities and invest in battery storage and home energy management solutions.

Former Indian cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni has invested in SolarSquare, the country's largest residential rooftop solar platform, through his family office Midas Deals. Alongside the investment, Dhoni has been appointed as the company's brand ambassador, according to reports on Monday.

The investment was made as part of SolarSquare's recently closed $53 million Series C funding round, led by B Capital. Lightspeed Venture Partners doubled down on its earlier commitment, while Elevation Capital, Lowercarbon Capital, NGP Capital, Rainmatter by Zerodha, and Good Capital also participated. The round takes SolarSquare's total capital raised past $100 million, according to Entrepreneur India.

A Growing Clean Energy Portfolio

The SolarSquare deal fits a clear pattern in Dhoni's investment strategy, which has increasingly tilted toward sustainability and clean technology. His family office has previously backed BluSmart, the electric vehicle ride-hailing platform, as well as EMotorad, a Pune-based electric bicycle startup where he also serves as investor and brand endorser. Other notable investments from Midas Deals include drone maker Garuda Aerospace, digital insurer ACKO, and game-tech studio LightFury Games.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=a1yZmLoIQ8g

Dhoni's dual role as investor and brand ambassador mirrors a model he has used with several portfolio companies, deploying his public profile alongside capital to accelerate consumer trust and market awareness.

"At the time, residential solar was still very nascent, with barely 1 lakh homes going solar per year."

SolarSquare's Rapid Ascent

Mumbai-headquartered SolarSquare was founded in 2015 by Shreya Mishra, Nikhil Nahar, and Neeraj Jain with the goal of simplifying rooftop solar adoption for Indian households. The company operates a vertically integrated model handling the entire customer journey, from consultation and system design to installation, financing support, and long-term maintenance.

https://www.instagram.com/p/CoZwAtWo8vV/

The startup has installed rooftop solar systems in more than 50,000 homes and approximately 400 housing societies across 29 cities in nine states, with over 150 megawatts of solar capacity deployed. Its annual revenue run rate now exceeds ₹1,000 crore (approximately $114 million), according to company disclosures.

"Five years ago, we made a conviction-led bet that every Indian home will be powered by rooftop solar. At the time, residential solar was still very nascent, with barely 1 lakh homes going solar per year. Today, the category has inflected with 1 lakh homes adopting solar every 10 days in India."

— Shreya Mishra, Co-Founder and CEO, SolarSquare

With the fresh capital, SolarSquare plans to enter 30 to 40 additional cities, enhance its technology platform, broaden financing options, and expand into battery storage and home energy management — areas that could transform the company from a solar installer into a comprehensive home energy brand.

India's Residential Solar Opportunity

The investment comes amid a surge in India's solar sector. The country became the world's third-largest solar power producer in 2025, behind China and the United States. Cumulative installed solar capacity has grown from roughly 3 gigawatts in 2014 to more than 150 gigawatts in 2026, supported by government incentives and subsidy schemes targeting rooftop adoption.

https://x.com/8M_Shailesh/status/2079460183521305028

India has set a target of 500 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2030, with solar expected to contribute more than half. Yet residential solar penetration remains below 5 percent, compared with 35 percent in Australia and 15 percent in Germany, despite an estimated 70 million viable residential rooftops.

"India's energy transition will not be won on the grid alone — it will be won home by home, city by city. SolarSquare combines category leadership, best-in-class unit economics, and a proprietary technology and asset-management layer that compounds with every install."

— Karan Mohla, General Partner, B Capital

Corporate funding in the solar sector rose to $11.1 billion across 53 deals in the first quarter of 2026, a 131 percent year-over-year increase, according to Mercom Capital Group. The sector has also attracted other Indian cricketers as investors, with Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma recently backing Hyderabad-based Truzon Solar.

What's Next

SolarSquare's Series C was valued at between $450 million and $500 million post-money, according to TechCrunch, more than doubling the roughly $200 million valuation at which Lightspeed led the company's $40 million Series B in December 2024. With Dhoni's celebrity backing and over $100 million in the bank, the startup is positioned to push residential solar deeper into India's mid-tier cities — a market where brand trust can make or break consumer adoption.
